title: Stroke of Fate
paragraphs: NBC's 1953 alternate-history anthology asks how history might have changed if a crucial event had ended differently, then dramatizes the imagined consequences of that turning point.

Thirteen-program NBC counterfactual-history anthology. Each episode dramatizes a historical turning point under a deliberately hypothetical changed outcome, followed in many broadcasts by historian/commentator framing or news.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: NBC counterfactual-history run (October 4, 1953 to December 27, 1953) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Lester Lewis (producer, conceiver, and writer), Mort Lewis (producer, conceiver, and writer), Fred Weihe (director), Lionel Ricou (announcer and performer), Ted Osborne (performer), Alexander Scourby (performer), and John Stanley (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

The stories often return to historical turning points and contingency, alternate history and counterfactual history, historian and expert commentary, war, military decisions and conquest, United States history, and political power, succession and statecraft.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Stroke of Fate counterfactual-history radio format, Stroke of Fate premise: Earl of Essex [followed by NBC News], Stroke of Fate premise: Escape of Marie Antoinette, and Stroke of Fate premise: Germany Invades the Rhineland.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]], [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]], [[show|the-chase|The Chase]], [[show|dimension-x|Dimension X]], and [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]].
